resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and Arabic source scope, review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review metadata, queue validation, typecheck, 79 test files with 462 tests, complete build, 39 IIS rules with 61 route cases, and 724 generated-link checks passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded Arabic pass identified 25 actionable defects in battery summaries, evidence notes, and safety wording; all 25 were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent Arabic human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted.

findings.summary: The removable-cell summary used repetitive wording.
evidence: The previous Arabic phrase repeated the idea of rechargeability and removability awkwardly.
findings.resolution: Rephrased it as a rechargeable, removable cell for compatible devices.

findings.summary: The integrated-battery summary did not clearly use a contrast with a replaceable cell.
evidence: The previous wording used ‘instead of’ without the clearest Arabic contrast for the safety-relevant distinction.
findings.resolution: Rephrased it as an internal pack, not a user-replaceable cell.

findings.summary: The approval note lacked a definite article for the associated research record.
evidence: The previous text was understandable but used an incomplete literal rendering of the record reference.
findings.resolution: Retained the date and clarified the associated research record reference.

findings.summary: The capacity note used less direct wording for the labeled capacity.
evidence: The previous text said the label suggested a value rather than stating the labeled capacity directly.
findings.resolution: Clarified that actual capacity is lower than the capacity indicated on the label.

findings.summary: The 20 A rating omitted the unit and used an incomplete sentence.
evidence: The previous text began with ‘20’ and did not identify amperes.
findings.resolution: Specified a continuous 20 A rating and excluded pulse ratings.

findings.summary: The independent comparison note omitted the unit and used awkward wrapper wording.
evidence: The previous text used a bare ‘20’ and a literal phrase for the exact wrapper.
findings.resolution: Rephrased it as a conservative independent 20 A comparison with the exact wrapper and production revision.

findings.summary: The exact-model note omitted the 15 A unit.
evidence: The previous Arabic text placed a bare ‘15’ before the description.
findings.resolution: Specified a conservative 15 A value from exact-model testing.

findings.summary: The technical term tabless was mistranslated as a table revision.
evidence: The previous text used Arabic for tables, changing the battery construction described by the source.
findings.resolution: Used a clear Arabic explanation with the protected technical term ‘tabless’.

findings.summary: The true continuous value omitted both amperage units.
evidence: The previous text used bare 36 and 56 values in a safety-relevant rating note.
findings.resolution: Specified 36 A continuous and temperature-limited 56 A.

findings.summary: The conservative rating omitted its 40 A unit.
evidence: The previous text began the rating with a bare ‘40’.
findings.resolution: Specified a conservative 40 A value and retained the pre-production and CCC caveat.

findings.summary: The recommended rating omitted its 13 A unit and used an awkward cycle-life phrase.
evidence: The previous text used a bare 13 and an unnatural literal translation of cycle life.
findings.resolution: Specified 13 A continuous and an absolute 16.8 A maximum not intended for cycle life.

findings.summary: The 70 A value was mistranslated as a temperature phrase without a unit.
evidence: The previous text said ‘70 temperature-limited’ and omitted the rating unit.
findings.resolution: Specified temperature-limited 70 A and retained the pre-production sample caveat.

findings.summary: The 70 A value was mistranslated as 70 ألف, changing the unit to thousands.
evidence: The previous Arabic number word ‘ألف’ means thousand rather than amperes.
findings.resolution: Restored the 70 A value and the temperature-control requirement.

findings.summary: The exact-wrapper note omitted the amperage units and degree symbol.
evidence: The previous text used bare 40 and ‘60 degrees Celsius’ in an uneven technical phrase.
findings.resolution: Specified the 40 A exact-wrapper value, 60 °C limit, and EVE 40PL rewrap.

findings.summary: The exact-sample note omitted the 19 A unit and used awkward repetition.
evidence: The previous text used a bare 19 and repeated the exact-testing idea unnaturally.
findings.resolution: Specified the conservative 19 A value and clarified the exact tested samples.

findings.summary: The 90 A value was mistranslated with an Arabic letter rather than the amperage unit.
evidence: The previous text used ‘90 أ’ and an ungrammatical temperature phrase.
findings.resolution: Specified temperature-limited 90 A and retained the pre-production caveat.

findings.summary: The 40 A rating omitted its unit and the production-continuity wording was awkward.
evidence: The previous text used a bare 40 and an unnatural literal phrase for unresolved continuity.
findings.resolution: Specified 40 A, temperature-limited 60 A, and unresolved production continuity.

findings.summary: The conservative value omitted its 40 A unit.
evidence: The previous text used a bare 40 in a technical rating statement.
findings.resolution: Specified the conservative 40 A value and retained the capacity and marking caveats.

findings.summary: The 13 A value omitted its unit and repeated an awkward exact-sample phrase.
evidence: The previous text used a bare 13 and unnatural wording for exact tested samples.
findings.resolution: Specified the conservative 13 A value and clarified the pre-production and CCC caveat.

findings.summary: The tester-estimated note omitted the 30 A unit and retained an English possessive.
evidence: The previous text used a bare 30 and the English phrase ‘Reliance's’.
findings.resolution: Specified the tester-estimated 30 A value and natural Arabic ownership wording.

findings.summary: The two-batch note omitted the 20 A and 30 A units.
evidence: The previous text used bare 20 and an Arabic letter for 30.
findings.resolution: Specified 20 A continuous and temperature-limited 30 A.

findings.summary: The continuous-versus-pulse statement omitted the unit and used an incomplete opening.
evidence: The previous text began with ‘12 continuous’ and used an Arabic letter for 20.
findings.resolution: Clarified 12 A continuous, 20 A pulse-only, and preserved the exact wrapper identifier.

findings.summary: The exact-wrapper note omitted the 20 A and 15 A units and used mixed technical wording.
evidence: The previous text used a bare 20 and translated the continuous recommendation inconsistently.
findings.resolution: Specified both current units and clarified the advertisement and later sourcing caveats.

findings.summary: The exact-model note omitted the 30 A unit and used an incomplete sourcing description.
evidence: The previous text used a bare 30 and did not clearly identify underlying cell sourcing.
findings.resolution: Specified the 30 A exact-model value and clarified possible wrapper and cell-source differences.

findings.summary: The five-leg revision note omitted the 30 A unit and used an awkward inheritance warning.
evidence: The previous text used a bare 30 and a literal phrase for materially different revisions.
findings.resolution: Specified 30 A and clarified that four-leg and later revisions must not inherit this profile.
